docomo2011.title: Damage and Restoration Status Regarding the Tohoku-Pacific Ocean Earthquake and Future Prospects — 2. Damage and restoration status of NTT DOCOMO, INC. ("DOCOMO")
docomo2011.author: NTT DOCOMO, INC. (in the NTT Group joint post-incident status release, with NTT, NTT East, NTT West and NTT Communications)
docomo2011.quote: After the earthquake struck, communications traffic increased dramatically and it was difficult for calls to get through. To address this, DOCOMO implemented maximum capacity restrictions on voice calls of 80 percent (90 percent in certain areas) around the Tohoku and Kanto regions to ensure that important communications could go through. In Miyagi prefecture, DOCOMO temporarily implemented maximum capacity restrictions on packet transmissions of 30 percent immediately after the earthquake, however, there has been no restrictions since.
quotes: Due to the impact of the Tohoku-Pacific Ocean Earthquake that occurred on March 11, 2011, some of NTT Group's services, including fixed-line and mobile communication services, remain unavailable, particularly in the Tohoku region. [cover page of the same 30 March 2011 release, url_cover, not the section-2 sub-page]
As of 5:00 p.m. on March 12 (JST), 6,720 stations were inoperable.

the regions eligible to post messages were expanded to cover the entire nation on March 17, and starting March 18, in addition to posting messages using i-mode, posting of messages from smartphones was also enabled. As of 12:00 midnight on March 28 (JST), the number of messages posted reached approximately 3.79 million.
supports: voice restriction of 80 percent, 90 percent in certain areas, across Tohoku and Kanto
packet restriction of 30 percent in Miyagi only, temporary, none afterwards
6,720 base stations inoperable as of 5:00 p.m. 12 March
Disaster Message Board opened nationwide 17 March; approximately 3.79 million posts by 28 March

mic2012.title: Maintaining Communications Capabilities during Major Natural Disasters and other Emergency Situations
mic2012.author: Hideo Tomioka, Deputy Director, Telecommunications Policy Division, Telecommunications Bureau, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Japan
mic2012.quote: Carriers restricted voice traffic by as much as 70 to 95 percent.* ... Packet traffic, however, was either not restricted or restricted at a lower rate than voice traffic. * There was 50 to 60 times the normal volume of traffic (DoCoMo).
quotes: Following the Great East Japan Earthquake, communications congestion (overload in telecommunications traffic) and communications blackouts occurred over a wide area. In response, Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) convened from April to December 2011 a study group to examine ways of securing the means of communication in emergency situations such as large-scale disasters.
The study group produced an interim report in July 2011 and a final report in December of the same year.
Extending the list of target institutions for emergency priority calls — Careful consideration based on a review of network design capacity
Introducing call length limits — Issue for future study
Introducing phone calls with reduced sound quality — Issue for future study

Mobile carriers are introducing emergency voice message services for sending voice messages via the packet network at times of disaster. (NTT DoCoMo introduced in March 2012 and KDDI plans to introduce in and after the spring of 2012.)

Overview of Alleviating Congestion in Emergency Situations. 1 Ensuring voice call capability. Upgrade the design capacity of facilities such as switches to improve overall communication capacity. Ensuring the stable viability of emergency priority calls.
supports: 50 to 60 times the normal volume of traffic (DoCoMo)
packet either not restricted or restricted at a lower rate than voice
carriers restricted mobile voice by as much as 70 to 95 percent
MIC study group April to December 2011, interim report July 2011, final report December 2011

final-report remedies: upgrade switch design capacity, ensure the stable viability of emergency priority calls, expand means of communication other than voice including voice messages over the packet network (DoCoMo March 2012). Extending the priority-call institution list was deferred, not adopted.
call length limits and reduced-quality calls deferred as issues for future study

slide 4 chart, maximum outgoing traffic restrictions by carrier: DoCoMo voice 90 percent and packet 30 percent, KDDI voice 95 and packet 0, SoftBank voice 70 and packet 0 — reconciles with DoCoMo’s own "80 percent (90 percent in certain areas)"

ntt2011apr.title: Restoration Status for Damage Caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Future Responses
ntt2011apr.author: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, NTT East, NTT DOCOMO, INC., NTT Communications Corporation
ntt2011apr.quote: NTT DOCOMO — Damage to base stations. Number of stations requiring restoration: 375 (including 68 stations within 30km radius surrounding the nuclear power plant). Fiscal year ended March 31, 2011: Approximately 6.0 billion yen (profit/loss). Fiscal year ending March 31, 2012 and onwards: Approximately 10.0 billion yen (CAPEX), Approximately 10.0 billion yen (profit/loss).
quotes: The financial impact including other NTT Group companies on the NTT Group consolidated financial results for the fiscal year ended March31, 2011 is approximately 30.0 billion yen (excluding donations)
supports: DOCOMO financial impact approximately 6.0 billion yen for the fiscal year ended 31 March 2011
NTT Group consolidated impact approximately 30.0 billion yen, excluding donations

unverified: That Ryuji Yamada was DoCoMo's president in March 2011. Named in the allocation sheet; no primary source was opened for it, so he does not appear in the prose or on a card.

That the restriction was applied through ITU-T Q.1248 automatic call gapping. Plausible and named in the allocation sheet, but no source was opened that names the mechanism, so the prose says only that one percentage was applied across the region and every attempt judged against it.
That voice connect rates fell to a few percent for days. No source opened states a connect or completion rate, so no connect-rate figure appears anywhere.

A MIC 'Intermediate Report on Maintaining Communications Capabilities during Major Disasters' dated 21 September 2011. The MIC presentation itself says the study group produced an interim report in July 2011 and a final report in December 2011, so the September date is not used.
Whether the 80 percent figure was applied uniformly to every switch in Tohoku and Kanto or varied by switch and by hour. The release states only the maximum.
The exact JST minute the earthquake struck. Only the date, 11 March 2011, is sourced here.

That the ministry recommended widening the emergency-priority-call list. The final report puts "Extending the list of target institutions for emergency priority calls" under "Careful consideration based on a review of network design capacity" — considered and deferred, not adopted — so the prose says only "emergency priority calls kept viable", the report’s own wording, and the deferral is stated on card c1.
Any venue for the MIC presentation. The title slide carries the date, the title and Tomioka’s MIC affiliation and no event name, so no venue is claimed.
That voice and packet restrictions ran on the same equipment or in the same instant. The releases give neither, so card c2 says only "same network, same days".
